title: Fine-tuning Laya on a laptop: 300 customer-service cases, Apple M3 Max
setup: 300 training cases (1,500 decisions: 1 choice, 1 score, 3 noul each) from the public LocalLLaMA/typed-decisions benchmark, customer_service workflow. 10% held out inside the run for calibration. A separate 100-case test split (500 decisions) evaluated with a fixed script before and after.
hardware: Apple M3 Max, 36 GB unified memory, PyTorch 2.14 mps backend, fp32
notes: Accuracy on the untouched 500-decision test split went from 0.376 to 0.712 after 54 minutes on a laptop GPU with 1,350 training decisions. The upstream checkpoint reached 0.766 with four times the data across all four workflows on two T4s.

Every primitive moved: choice 0.26 → 0.71, score 0.36 → 0.71, noul 0.65 → 0.73. The base model was worst exactly where option descriptions are domain specific (choice), which is where labelled data helps most.
Mean proper-score reward roughly halved in magnitude (−1.12 → −0.59): the model is not just picking the right option more often, its whole distribution is closer to the teacher's.

Calibration error barely changed (0.121 → 0.118) because the base checkpoint's shipped temperatures were already refitted per type; the new fit landed at 1.02, 1.22 and 1.79 for choice, score and noul.
The loss printed by the RLCD loop is noisy by design (it mixes a zero-mean policy-gradient term with a cross-entropy term), so watch the held-out metrics rather than the loss.
The saved checkpoint is fp32 (1.7 GB). Convert to fp16 for serving if disk matters; answers are unchanged within rounding.
